articles.title: A record market high is not a reason to change your investment plans
articles.dek: If you are growing your wealth , few things do more for your financial future than owning assets that are expected to outpace inflation. What the investment science advocates is unglamorous enough: contribute to a diversified portfolio matched to the rate of return your plan actually requires, and if a lump sum arrives, put it to work promptly so that compounding starts sooner. Then the market touches a record, and something happens to otherwise sensible people. Money that was headed for a portfolio finds a reason to sit in a deposit account for another month or two, until things settle down.
